item.title: Where would I publish work about regular human characters?: Re: Where would I publish work about regular human characters?
item.content:encoded:
I want to know if there's a place for this or if this is to be kept solely in the tales and not have a description page

If you're looking to just have an overview of laundry-list information and statistics pertaining to recurring character, the closest the site has is a series hub page. For example, the Kiryu Labs Hub.

That said, if you want to have a hub page, you need to have tales to populate the hub first.

item.title: Do tales need to be greenlit if they are your first article?: Re: Do tales need to be greenlit if they are your first article?
item.content:encoded: In the strictest of terms you don't need to be greenlit to post anything. However, greenlights allow you to use the Feedback and Critique Forum which you will probably want to use because it's the easiest place to get crit on your article. Tales, just like SCPs and GoI Formats, require two greenlights before being posted to the Feedback and Critique Forum.

item.title: SCP Radio saves handlers for feet pics: Re: Admin Post - Info - Open
item.content:encoded:
I didn't say I wasn't looking for concept critique

If you want critique on a concept, please follow the template noted in the Ideas Critique forum required reading, and do not provide a sandbox draft unless a reviewer asks to read a full draft.

If you're expecting reviewers to read your sandbox draft before providing critique, you can ask for draft feedback in the IRC chatrooms. Greenlights are not required there, though some reviewers may still ask authors to first go through the greenlighting process if the core concept needs revision before the draft itself can be fixed.

item.title: SCP instance naming: Re: SCP instance naming
item.content:encoded: Thank you! This answers my question perfectly.

item.title: SCP instance naming: Re: SCP instance naming
item.content:encoded:
so what exactly is this for?

Basically any sort of specific thing that is related to a primary anomaly, but distinct enough to make more sense to mention specifically. So if the Foundation was containing an anomalous field and there was an anomalous rabbit that only shows up in that field, the field would be SCP-XXXX and the rabbit would be SCP-XXXX-1. That helps prevent confusion/strange sentences where it would make sense to refer to only one thing at a time (for example, "SCP-XXXX-1 consumes solely dandelion greens" makes sense for the rabbit, not the field).

additionally I'm wondering if something like SCP-XXXX-1-1 would be acceptable or if it should just be referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

It depends on what relationship that something has to SCP-XXXX-1. You would use an offshoot that has an existing designation offshoot number if you're referring to a specific part of that previously designated thing. To use the previous example, if the rabbit carried a good luck charm that had its own anomalous properties, that might be SCP-XXXX-1-1, though I think most authors would use SCP-XXXX-1-A or SCP-XXXX-1a or the like.

So basically:

  • SCP-XXXX: main anomaly/main collection of anomalies the Foundation is containing
  • SCP-XXXX-1: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX
  • SCP-XXXX-1-A: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX-1
  • and so on.

I have no specific ideas that would entail using the SCP-XXXX-1-1 designation but I'd like to know if such a thing could be used and in which circumstances.

item.title: Quasi-Rewrites: Re: Quasi-Rewrites
item.content:encoded:
SCP-4166 exists which means that writing things like SCP-4166 is totally viable. Go ahead.

The original SCP you want to reinterpret is licensed CC BY-SA. You can do whatever you like so long as you credit the author. I don't think it's plagiarism unless you claim the idea as your own, or copy the text verbatim?

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?: Re: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.content:encoded:
I don't want to bea nudge about this, but I also had an idea to make this a joke SCP and I just want to run the idea to see if it's actually funny or if it's just me.

There are multiple instances of SCP-2806, and multiple instances can be designated by number or letter. In this case they are numbered, but that's for the instances when they are not connected to a human, so what if the humans still connected were designated by letter?

So my guy comes in, clearly a Mary Sue, the data entry worker checks the file and sees that about 200 of these guys could be coming through and decides to designate this instance 2806-J just so he can be purposely misfiled as a joke SCP even though he's not a joke. So the real joke is that he's actually totally legit but nobody takes him seriously because of a prank in records and his career is ruined.

I honestly don't know whether that's funny enough to work, so feel free to shoot it down.

item.title: My first SCP article: Re: My first SCP article
item.content:encoded:
No, Satan's appearance wasn't mentioned in the Bible (I read the whole thing, I know) that's why I attributed it to Scapegoats, it's the only mention of goats and sin so I connected the dots.

The goats die at the end of the ritual? Since when has death stopped an SCP? One word: Undead. The weight of the sins won't let their souls rest, so even though they died, they rise again, that's why they have to be contained, the GOC tried killing them but it totally did not work at all.

Actually, the mountain thing is better, now I have a location where they can be contained, much more important than an angel.

Again, sorry if it came off as anti-semitic, "sins of the nation of Israel" came from how it was worded in the Bible. I just wanted to give an origin to the demon goat archetype that made sense to me. But whatever, I have other ideas, either we work out the kinks or I drop it to the bottom of the list and pick a different one. I just wanted to see what would get attention. But if you hate it, that's not the attention I want.

Now that I know what you don't like, was there one on my list you did like and would rather I focus on instead?
